key_insight: Requential coding compresses a model by recording which self-generated training samples a teacher chooses, yielding codes whose length reflects what the model actually learns rather than its parameter count or the raw entropy of the data.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical compression-and-generalization lens for large AI systems, enabling tighter PAC-Bayes bounds and more informative comparisons across model scale, ensembles, and training regimes.
method: Teacher samples from the student’s own distribution.
The code stores only the teacher’s selections, charging bits mainly when teacher and student disagree.
This avoids both parameter-size-driven quantization costs and the full-data costs of prequential coding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that requential codes are often orders of magnitude shorter than prequential codes, improve with scale, and produce state-of-the-art PAC-Bayes generalization guarantees for billion-parameter LLMs.
watch_item: The approach depends on a teacher-student sampling procedure, so its practical benefit may be sensitive to how well the teacher can probe the student distribution and to the cost of generating/selecting samples.
paper_title: Requential Coding: Pushing the Limits of Model Compression with Self-Generated Training Data
